_comment: What the C# air arm actually does, recorded so 2d's second half is ported
against a measurement instead of against the code read out loud.
Four seeds, each run twice - once with no air at all - because bombs draw
on Army's own _rng, so an air pass and a no-air pass on one seed do NOT
share a ground battle and the difference cannot be read off one run.
The control is the point of the no-air passes: noair-20260901 is
config-identical to passes.core-size-reinforce in csharp-army.json, and
reproduces all nineteen of its rows to the digit (n, z and spread, four
groups a row). The harness is therefore the same harness, and the air
numbers below are measured against a ground fight already accepted.

setup.seed_note: four seeds; the first is the recording's own

_findings: 1. AIR IS NOT AN EVENT, IT IS WEATHER. Battlefield's comment says one
sortie every twenty-odd seconds per side is 'an event you look up
for'. Measured: at least one gunship is airborne for 69-93% of the
round, two at a time on every seed, because both sides' clocks start
at zero and 17 s of cadence against a ~17 s transit is continuous
cover, not a visit.
2. A THIRD OF EVERY BOMB LOAD LANDS OFF THE FIELD, and all of it in x,
none in z. A bomb is released while |x| < 92, inherits 30 m/s along
the gunship's own track and falls from 19 m, so it is thrown 56-62 m
downrange: measured landings reach |x| = 148-154 against a field that
ends at 92. 9-16 bombs a round, 26-42%, land on nobody by
construction - the gate is on the release point and the bomb is not
released where it lands.
3. THE FIRST SORTIE OF EVERY ROUND IS WASTED. Both armies spawn at
|z| = 77 and the gunships fly the seam at |z| = 17-35; first killing
bomb is t = 16.7-26.4 s, and 13-15 bombs are spent before t=30 for
5-15 riflemen between them. Air only bites once the lines meet.
4. BOMBS ARE THE PRIMARY INFANTRY KILLER, by a distance. 60-76 riflemen
a round to bombs against 16-37 to rifles, one bomb worth 11-23 men at
its best because squads clump inside a 16 m circle. Against armour it
is the opposite: 9-12 tanks of 55-63 lost, a 15-22% share.
5. AIR KILLS ITS OWN. 11-29 of the riflemen a bomb kills are the
dropper's side - 18-42% of them - because the blast circle does not
ask whose men are inside it and the lines meet at the seam.
6. THE GROUND FIGHT ABSORBS ALL OF IT. Armour lost rises 54-60 to 55-63
and the exit headcounts are unchanged (8-11 of 12 a side, 32-36
infantry of 36): replacement covers 60-76 dead riflemen a round
without the establishment moving. Air changes who dies, not how the
round ends.
7. TWO DEFECTS THE PORT MUST NOT COPY BLIND. Detonate has no hp check on
the armour loop and RemoveAll only runs at the end of Update, so a
tank killed earlier in the same frame can fire Destroyed twice;
measured over 4 x 90 s it never happened (doubleFire 0/0 on every
seed), so it is a latent defect, not a live one. And SendHelicopter's
direction is drawn from UnityEngine.Random rather than Army._rng: in
the C# the air arm is not reproducible from an Army seed at all.

_comment: Across the four seeds. A port matching inside these is the air
arm; matching one seed to the digit is not asked for and is not
possible - the C# sortie clock is not on the army's seed.
